On Tue, Jun 1, 2027 at 09:45 AM monica_patel@redwood.ai wrote:
> Vivek — can eng confirm whether the new quant profile triggers a different kernel selection/exec path that could cause extra micro-batching or KV cache thrash?

Investigation notes (initial):
- Root cause appears to be the combination of the q4_0-mem-optim profile + the runtime kernel auto-selector. The new profile nudges the selector to an int8-like kernel path we recently added; that path adds an extra small CPU pre/post-process step for KV marshaling on sequences >512 which increases end-to-end latency and occasionally times out in our existing retry window.
- We also found an off-by-one in attention mask handling for compiled kernels under specific token alignments; that leads to sparse 500s (invalid attention shapes) for a narrow subset of inputs — precisely what Hightide's checkout prompts trigger.

Immediate mitigations considered:
1) Canary rollback: switch 20% of Hightide traffic back to rw-instruct-v2-q3_0 + q3 profile (no kernel change) — should cut p95 immediately.
2) Runtime toggle: force previous kernel selection for the q4 profile (fast but riskier).
3) Hotfix to compiled attention mask (will require a short deploy, ~3–4 hours testing).

I recommend (1) now, (3) as next step with priority patch. I'll prepare a runtime patch and a rollback playbook. Attaching a diff for the patch we intend to test.

—Vivek Kulkarni
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime
